newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian GIMV to float up to 19.9 pct from June 26.
newsitem.headline: Belgian GIMV to float up to 19.9 pct from June 26.

text.p: GIMV, the investment company of the Flemish regional government, said on Tuesday a maximum 19.9 percent of its capital would be listed on the Brussels stock exchange from June 26.
GIMV, Flanders' largest venture capital company, said in the prospectus on the IPO, presented at a roadshow, that the Flemish region would put in 14.8 percent of its shares.
Institutional shareholders are invited to offer 5.1 percent.
"So the placement would relate to a maximum of 4,599,770 shares, or 19.9 percent of GIMV's capital," the prospectus said.

The Flemish region, which will still have some 70 percent in GIMV after the IPO, agreed not to sell any additional GIMV stock before January 1999. By law, the region's stake cannot drop below 50.1 percent.

The prospectus said that after the "lock-up" period ending in January 1999, GIMV will request the listing of another 4.7 percent held by banks ASLK/CGER and Credit Communal de Belgique and 10.6 percent held by institutional investors.

The fixed price will be announced on June 10 at the latest after book-building with institutionals in a private placement beginning June 4. Book-building will take place within a price range of 1,920 and 2,250 francs.
Shares will be offered to private investors from June 10. Subscriptions to the offer, managed by a consortium of KB Securities, ASLK/CGER Bank and Bank Degroof, close on June 17 at the latest.
The Flemish government, which now owns 85 percent of GIMV, decided last year to float around 15 percent. Another 15 percent is already in private hands after a private placement in 1995.
The main interests of GIMV include 33.99 percent of Belgian electronics firm Barco, 9.99 percent of engineering company BMT and a small interest in Nasdaq-listed software firm Xeikon.

It is a shareholder in Europe's Easdaq growth stocks market and in Belgian telecommunications group Telenet, which aims to convert Flanders' cable television network to provide multimedia and voice telephone services from 1998.
Telenet Operaties NV is a unit of Telenet Holding NV, which is 25 percent-owned by U.S. West International and 20 percent by GIMV.

"Investing in GIMV shares is an investment in dynamic Flemish and international companies which are not normally quoted on the stock exchange," chairman Raynier van Outryve d'Ydewalle told a news conference.
He noted GIMV was cooperating with venture capital companies in Europe, Asia and the United States.
GIMV's bourse listing had been in the pipeline for years.

Last year the plan hit a snag over what the company should do with its cash mountain -- due principally to the sale last year of interests in Belgian companies such as Plant Genetic Systems, Lernout & Hauspie and Innogenetics.
The sales gave GIMV a combined capital gain of 5.09 billion francs, which represented the bulk of the company's 5.65 billion franc 1996 group net profit.
Managing director Gerard Van Acker said he expected GIMV to have 1997 net profit of at least 1.5 billion francs.
He noted GIMV was a healthy company free of debt and expected investments to rise further in 1997.
"We are planning a few important investments in growth capital," he said. Divestments by contrast would be modest.
"We do not foresee any major capital gains or divestments (this year)," he said.

Van Outrive d'Ydewalle said GIMV now had a cash hoard of 8.6 billion francs, which could be used mainly to support companies offering innovative products or servies or wanted to develop their foreign markets.
He said GIMV should be seen as a growth stock but one with a clear dividend policy. GIMV is paying a 1996 dividend per share of 43 francs against 30 francs in 1995.
A research report by KB Securities, Banque Degroof and ASLK/CGER, put net asset value at 2,267 francs, with Barco accounting for 50.3 percent.
-- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815
